questions.text: In FastAPI, how do you specify that an endpoint handler should run asynchronously without blocking the event loop?
options: Use the @async_route decorator
Define the handler function with 'async def'
Wrap the return value in asyncio.Future()
Set background_task=True in router configuration
questions.explanation: Declaring endpoint functions with 'async def' allows FastAPI to execute them cooperatively on the asyncio event loop.

questions.text: What does Pydantic BaseModel primarily provide when used in FastAPI request bodies?
options: Database connection pooling
Data validation, parsing, and automated OpenAPI documentation schema generation
Automatic SQL query generation and ORM mapping
Client-side cookie storage encryption
questions.explanation: Pydantic performs runtime data type validation, sanitization, and produces OpenAPI/Swagger schemas.

questions.text: Which dependency injection tool in FastAPI is used to share authentication, database sessions, and permissions across routes?
options: fastapi.Depends
fastapi.Inject
fastapi.Provide
fastapi.Autowired
questions.explanation: Depends() is FastAPI's standard mechanism for dependency declaration and hierarchical resolution.

questions.text: How should long-running CPU-intensive or slow operations be handled without starving FastAPI async requests?
options: Execute them synchronously in the main async function
Offload them to BackgroundTasks, Celery worker, or run in a thread pool via run_in_executor
Increase the OS thread stack size
Set async_timeout to 0
questions.explanation: Blocking operations block the GIL and asyncio loop unless dispatched to worker threads or external task queues.

questions.text: What is the primary architectural purpose of Row Level Security (RLS) in PostgreSQL?
options: Compressing table rows on disk to save storage
Restricting which rows a database user or session can select, update, or delete based on SQL policies
Creating read-only replicas across multiple geographical regions
Automatically converting JSON fields into B-Trees
questions.explanation: RLS applies security filters directly in the database engine, preventing unauthorized row leakage regardless of application flaws.

questions.text: When establishing a relationship where each Job Listing requires multiple skills with custom weights, which relational pattern is ideal?
options: A single CSV column in the jobs table
A junction / associative table (job_required_skills) with foreign keys to jobs and skills
Duplicate job rows for every single skill
Store unindexed text blobs
questions.explanation: An associative table allows clean Many-to-Many mappings, relational integrity, indexing, and per-skill metadata such as weight.

questions.text: What type of index is most effective in PostgreSQL for high-speed lookup on an exact UUID primary key?
options: B-Tree index (default)
GIN full-text index
BRIN index
Spatial R-Tree index
questions.explanation: B-Tree indexes provide logarithmic O(log N) lookups and are the default standard index for equality lookups.

questions.text: What is the consequence of adding 'ON DELETE CASCADE' to a foreign key constraint from job_applications to candidates?
options: Candidate deletion will fail if applications exist
Deleting the candidate profile automatically purges all related application records
The foreign key is converted into a loose pointer
Candidate records become anonymous
questions.explanation: ON DELETE CASCADE propagates the delete operation to dependent child rows automatically.

questions.text: Why is using ES Modules ('import' / 'export' with type='module') advantageous in modern vanilla web apps?
options: It eliminates the need for any CSS styling
It enables scoped modular code without global variable collisions and supports native browser loading
It forces synchronous execution of all scripts
It prevents fetch requests from failing
questions.explanation: ES Modules provide isolated scopes, strict mode enforcement, and clean code organization without global namespace pollution.

questions.text: Which CSS layout method is best suited for a 2-dimensional dashboard grid with responsive sidebar and main content?
options: Float layout with clearfix
CSS Grid (grid-template-columns / grid-template-rows)
Inline-block elements with vertical-align
Table elements
questions.explanation: CSS Grid is purpose-built for two-dimensional structured dashboard layouts with seamless responsive adaptability.

questions.text: How can a web app detect when a candidate navigates away or switches browser tabs during an active proctored assessment?
options: Listen to 'visibilitychange' on document and 'blur' on window
Inspect the user's desktop taskbar via navigator
Read local process memory through WebSocket
Check screen brightness values
questions.explanation: Document visibilitychange and window blur events reliably detect when the user minimizes the tab or switches apps.

questions.text: What is the key advantage of client-side optimistic UI updates combined with API synchronization?
options: It eliminates the need for a database
It provides instant, zero-latency feedback to the user while keeping server data consistent
It automatically solves all network outages permanently
It bypasses authentication requirements
questions.explanation: Optimistic UI immediately reflects user actions on screen while performing asynchronous network requests in the background.

questions.text: When building an AI Startup Copilot, why should the backend enforce structured JSON schema validation on LLM output?
options: To prevent the browser from having to parse text and guarantee predictable UI rendering of fields like risks and assumptions
Because LLMs cannot output plain English
To reduce cloud server electricity consumption
To encrypt the prompt tokens
questions.explanation: Enforcing structured JSON guarantees that downstream frontend components receive guaranteed typed fields without parser crashes.

questions.text: Why must AI API keys (such as OpenAI, Gemini, or Anthropic keys) NEVER be exposed in browser client JavaScript?
options: Browsers do not support UTF-8 characters
Any user can inspect network traffic or source code, steal the key, and rack up unauthorized API bills
API keys slow down CSS rendering
The browser console will automatically deactivate the key
questions.explanation: Client-side secrets are fully accessible to end users; API credentials must strictly reside on the secured backend.

questions.text: According to the Idea2Impact architectural principles, how should AI-generated evaluations and startup risks be treated?
options: As infallible guarantees of financial success or failure
As assistive decision support for human judgment, clearly labeled with assumptions rather than certainty
As legal binding contracts for venture capital
As automatic rejections for startup founders
questions.explanation: AI models provide decision support and summarize assumptions, but human judgment remains the ultimate authority.

questions.text: What is the purpose of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) in corporate candidate or startup discovery?
options: Grounding model responses in verifiable database documents and private profiles to prevent hallucinations
Replacing all SQL database tables with text embeddings
Converting PDFs to image files
Compressing video streams
questions.explanation: RAG retrieves specific facts and profiles from verified databases before prompting the model, anchoring the generation in real data.

questions.text: What is the primary difference between a 'struct' and a 'class' in C++?
options: A class can have member functions, but a struct cannot
Members and base classes are public by default in a struct, but private by default in a class
A struct is always allocated on the stack, while a class is always allocated on the heap
Classes support inheritance, but structs do not in C++
questions.explanation: In C++, the only semantic difference between struct and class is default access specification: public for struct, private for class.

questions.text: Why must a base class destructor almost always be declared as 'virtual' in C++?
options: To prevent memory leaks by ensuring the derived class destructor is called when deleting via a base pointer
To make the class pure abstract
To allow the destructor to accept parameters
To prevent the compiler from generating a default constructor
questions.explanation: Deleting a derived class object through a base class pointer without a virtual destructor causes undefined behavior and resource leaks.

questions.text: What programming idiom does modern C++ rely on where resource management is tied to object lifetime?
options: Garbage Collection (GC)
Resource Acquisition Is Initialization (RAII)
Lazy Evaluation Pipeline
Singleton Allocation
questions.explanation: RAII ensures resources like heap memory, file handles, and mutex locks are released automatically when the holding object goes out of scope.

questions.text: What is the key advantage of 'std::unique_ptr' over 'std::shared_ptr'?
options: std::unique_ptr has zero runtime overhead compared to a raw pointer and cannot be copied, guaranteeing single ownership
std::unique_ptr can be shared across multiple threads simultaneously
std::unique_ptr uses reference counting
std::unique_ptr cannot be moved
questions.explanation: std::unique_ptr enforces exclusive ownership with zero overhead (no control block or atomic reference counting).

questions.text: What happens when you pass a large std::vector into a function as 'void process(const std::vector<int>& vec)'?
options: A deep copy of all elements is allocated on the heap
It is passed by constant reference without copying, preventing unnecessary allocations while preventing modification
It causes a compilation error because vectors cannot be const
The vector is moved and invalidated in the caller
questions.explanation: Passing by 'const std::vector<int>&' avoids deep copying large arrays while enforcing read-only semantics.

questions.text: What is the output behavior of mutable default arguments in Python, e.g. 'def append_to(item, target=[])'?
options: A new empty list is created on every function call
The same list instance is reused across multiple calls because default argument expressions are evaluated once at definition time
Python raises a SyntaxError at runtime
The list is garbage collected immediately upon function return
questions.explanation: Default arguments are evaluated once when the function definition is executed, so mutable objects like lists or dicts persist state across calls.

questions.text: What is the primary function of the Global Interpreter Lock (GIL) in standard CPython?
options: To prevent multi-threaded network sockets
A mutex that protects access to Python objects, preventing multiple native threads from executing Python bytecodes concurrently
To automatically compile Python to machine bytecode ahead of time
To enforce typing discipline across imported modules
questions.explanation: CPython's GIL simplifies memory management by ensuring only one thread executes Python bytecode at a time.

questions.text: How do generator functions using the 'yield' keyword differ from functions that return a list?
options: Generators produce items lazily on-demand one at a time, requiring O(1) memory instead of holding all items in memory
Generators run on a separate CPU thread automatically
Generators cannot be iterated over with a for loop
Generators are slower and deprecated in Python 3.10+
questions.explanation: Generators compute elements lazily via the iterator protocol, resulting in huge memory savings for large datasets.

questions.text: What does the '@functools.wraps(func)' decorator do when creating custom decorators?
options: It turns the decorated function into an async coroutine
It preserves original metadata like __name__, __doc__, and annotations of the wrapped function
It encrypts the bytecode of the function
It makes the function run 2x faster
questions.explanation: functools.wraps copies the function name, docstring, and annotations from the original function to the wrapper.

questions.text: Which built-in Python data structure provides average O(1) time complexity for lookup, insertion, and deletion?
options: list
dict (and set)
tuple
collections.deque
questions.explanation: Python dicts and sets are implemented using hash tables, giving average O(1) key lookups, inserts, and deletes.

questions.text: What is the fundamental difference between '==' and '.equals()' when comparing objects in Java?
options: '==' compares object references (memory address), while '.equals()' tests for logical value equality (when overridden)
'==' compares content, while '.equals()' compares memory address
'==' only works on primitive integers
There is no difference between them in modern Java
questions.explanation: The '==' operator checks if two references point to the exact same memory address, whereas equals() is overridden to compare meaningful content.

questions.text: In Java 8+, what is a Functional Interface?
options: An interface with no methods at all
An interface that contains exactly one abstract method, suitable as the assignment target for a lambda expression
An interface that can only extend abstract classes
A class marked with the 'final' keyword
questions.explanation: A functional interface has exactly one abstract method (annotated optionally with @FunctionalInterface) and can be instantiated via lambdas.

questions.text: What does the 'volatile' keyword signify when declared on a Java field?
options: The variable cannot be changed once initialized
Reads and writes go directly to main memory, ensuring changes made by one thread are immediately visible to all other threads
The variable is stored on the call stack
The variable is serialized automatically
questions.explanation: The volatile modifier prevents thread caching of variables in CPU registers, establishing a happens-before memory visibility guarantee.

questions.text: What is the time complexity of retrieving a value by key in a well-distributed Java 'HashMap'?
options: O(n)
O(log n)
O(1) average time complexity
questions.explanation: HashMap computes hash buckets for keys, achieving average O(1) performance for get() and put() operations.

questions.text: Which exception type in Java must either be declared in a method's 'throws' clause or caught in a 'try-catch' block?
options: Checked Exceptions (subclasses of java.lang.Exception excluding RuntimeException)
Unchecked Exceptions (subclasses of RuntimeException)
Errors (like OutOfMemoryError)
AssertionError
questions.explanation: Checked exceptions are verified at compile-time and must be handled or declared in the method signature.

questions.text: What is a 'closure' in JavaScript?
options: A function bundled together with references to its surrounding lexical environment, allowing it to access outer variables even after the outer function has returned
A method that closes an active network connection
An IIFE (Immediately Invoked Function Expression) that returns undefined
A technique to prevent object mutation using Object.freeze()
questions.explanation: A closure gives an inner function access to an outer function's scope even after the outer function has finished executing.

questions.text: In the JavaScript Event Loop, which tasks have higher priority and run first after the current synchronous script completes?
options: Macrotasks (e.g., setTimeout, setInterval)
Microtasks (e.g., Promise.then/catch/finally, queueMicrotask)
DOM requestAnimationFrame callbacks
Disk I/O event handlers
questions.explanation: The microtask queue is drained completely before the event loop picks the next macrotask from the task queue.

questions.text: What is the difference between 'let'/'const' and 'var' regarding scoping in JavaScript?
options: 'let' and 'const' are block-scoped and temporal dead zone (TDZ) aware, while 'var' is function-scoped and hoisted with undefined
'var' is block-scoped, while 'let' is globally scoped
'const' values can never have their internal object properties modified
There is no difference in ES6+
questions.explanation: 'let' and 'const' respect block boundaries ({ ... }) and cannot be accessed before declaration (Temporal Dead Zone).

questions.text: What does 'Promise.all([p1, p2, p3])' do if any one of the promises rejects?
options: It waits for all others to finish, then returns the successful values
It immediately rejects with the reason of the first promise that rejected (fail-fast behavior)
It silently ignores the error and returns null
It converts the error into an undefined resolution
questions.explanation: Promise.all rejects immediately upon the first rejected promise; use Promise.allSettled if you need results for all promises regardless of outcome.

questions.text: What is the value of 'typeof null' in JavaScript, and why?
options: 'null'
'undefined'
'object' (a historic legacy bug in JS since its first implementation)
'boolean'
questions.explanation: In JavaScript's initial implementation, values had a type tag where 0 represented an object reference, and null was represented as the NULL pointer (0x00).

questions.text: In C, what is the effect of calling 'free(ptr)' on dynamically allocated memory?
options: It frees the allocated block back to the heap manager, but the pointer variable 'ptr' still holds the address (becoming a dangling pointer)
It sets 'ptr' to NULL automatically
It zeroes out the contents of the memory before freeing
It frees all other pointers that were referencing that memory
questions.explanation: free() releases the heap memory block, but does not modify the pointer variable itself; best practice is to set ptr = NULL immediately.

questions.text: What happens in pointer arithmetic when you increment an 'int*' pointer (ptr++) on a 64-bit architecture where sizeof(int) is 4 bytes?
options: The pointer address increases by 1 byte
The pointer address increases by 4 bytes (the size of the pointed-to type)
The pointer address increases by 8 bytes
The pointer address doubles
questions.explanation: Pointer arithmetic advances addresses by the size of the underlying type: ptr + 1 advances by sizeof(*ptr) bytes.

questions.text: What is the difference between 'malloc()' and 'calloc()' in the C standard library?
options: 'malloc' allocates uninitialized memory (contents are garbage), while 'calloc' zeroes out all allocated memory bytes
'malloc' allocates memory on the stack, while 'calloc' allocates on the heap
'calloc' can only allocate single primitive variables
'malloc' automatically runs destructors
questions.explanation: calloc(n, size) initializes all allocated bytes to zero; malloc(bytes) leaves memory uninitialized.

questions.text: What does the 'static' keyword do when applied to a global variable or function in a C source file?
options: It makes the variable thread-safe
It restricts the visibility (linkage) to the translation unit (.c file) where it is defined, preventing name collisions across files
It forces the compiler to place the variable in the CPU L1 cache
It prevents the variable from being modified
questions.explanation: Static global variables and functions have internal linkage and cannot be accessed from other object files.

questions.text: What is undefined behavior (UB) in C?
options: Code that always crashes with a segmentation fault
Constructs where the C standard imposes no requirements; the compiler may generate any instructions, optimize away checks, or produce arbitrary results
A syntax error caught by the preprocessor
A memory allocation that exceeds 4GB
questions.explanation: Undefined behavior means the C specification does not define what should happen, allowing compilers to assume it never happens during optimization.

questions.text: Why should developers use semantic HTML tags (<article>, <nav>, <header>, <main>) instead of generic <div> tags?
options: They render in 3D in modern web browsers
They provide meaningful document structure that enhances SEO, search indexing, and assistive screen reader accessibility (a11y)
They automatically disable CSS styling overrides
They make network downloads 50% faster
questions.explanation: Semantic tags convey meaning to search engine crawlers and assistive accessibility technologies, creating accessible landmarks.

questions.text: What is the purpose of the '<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">' tag in an HTML document?
options: To enable WebGL hardware acceleration
To configure the viewport dimensions and zoom level for responsive rendering across mobile and desktop devices
To set the browser tab favicon
To prevent users from right-clicking on the webpage
questions.explanation: The viewport meta tag ensures mobile browsers match the device screen width instead of pretending to be a 980px desktop browser.

questions.text: Which HTML form attribute prevents form submission if an input field is empty?
options: validate="true"
required
not-null
enforce
questions.explanation: The boolean attribute 'required' instructs the browser to enforce that the form control must have a value before submission.

questions.text: What does the 'alt' attribute on an '' tag accomplish?
options: Specifies alternative text for screen readers and when the image fails to load
Provides a tooltip when hovering over the image
Defines the CSS alignment of the image
Specifies a fallback image URL
questions.explanation: The alt attribute provides alternative text for accessibility (screen readers) and renders when the image resource cannot be loaded.

questions.text: What is the key difference between '<script src="app.js" async>' and '<script src="app.js" defer>'?
options: 'async' executes as soon as it is downloaded (potentially out-of-order), while 'defer' executes after HTML parsing completes in document order
'defer' downloads synchronously, while 'async' downloads asynchronously
'async' only works for module scripts, while 'defer' is for classical scripts
There is no difference in modern browsers
questions.explanation: Both download asynchronously without blocking HTML parsing; 'defer' guarantees execution in source order after DOM parsing finishes.

questions.text: What is the key difference between CSS Flexbox and CSS Grid?
options: Flexbox is designed for 1-dimensional layouts (rows OR columns), while CSS Grid is designed for 2-dimensional layouts (rows AND columns simultaneously)
Flexbox is only for mobile layouts, Grid is only for desktop layouts
Grid cannot center elements vertically
Flexbox requires JavaScript polyfills
questions.explanation: Flexbox manages distribution along a single axis (row or column), while CSS Grid coordinates tracks across two dimensions.

questions.text: What is the benefit of setting 'box-sizing: border-box;' globally in CSS?
options: Element width and height include padding and borders, preventing layout blowouts when adding padding
It makes borders rounded automatically
It removes margins between elements
It makes all elements display as block elements
questions.explanation: With border-box, the specified width includes content, padding, and border, making sizing predictable and calculations intuitive.

questions.text: Which CSS selector has the highest specificity?
options: div.nav-link:hover
#main-header
ul li.active
button[type='submit']
questions.explanation: An ID selector (#main-header) has specificity (1, 0, 0), which beats any combination of classes, attributes, or element selectors.

questions.text: How do CSS Custom Properties (Variables) defined with '--brand-color: #6366F1;' differ from Sass/SCSS variables?
options: CSS variables are dynamic, live in the browser DOM cascade, and can be updated at runtime via JavaScript or media queries
CSS variables cannot be inherited by children
CSS variables require a build step to compile
CSS variables only work for colors
questions.explanation: CSS variables are live DOM variables that cascade, inherit, and can be altered dynamically in JavaScript via element.style.setProperty().

questions.text: What CSS rule centers a child element both horizontally and vertically inside a flex container?
options: display: flex; justify-content: center; align-items: center;
display: flex; text-align: center; float: center;
display: flex; margin: auto center;
display: flex; vertical-align: middle;
questions.explanation: justify-content: center aligns along the main axis; align-items: center aligns along the cross axis.

questions.text: Why must you NOT call React Hooks inside loops, conditions, or nested functions?
options: React relies on the call order of hooks to preserve state identity across consecutive component re-renders
Hooks are converted to class methods during compilation
It causes memory leaks in the browser V8 engine
React hooks are asynchronous
questions.explanation: The Rules of Hooks enforce top-level execution so React can match each hook with its internal fiber linked list by execution order.

questions.text: What happens if you omit the dependency array in 'useEffect(() => { ... })'?
options: The effect only runs once when the component mounts
The effect runs on initial mount AND after EVERY single render of the component
The effect never runs
React throws a compile error
questions.explanation: No dependency array means the effect executes after every render. An empty array [] runs once on mount; [dep] runs when dep changes.

questions.text: What is the purpose of the 'key' prop when rendering lists of elements in React?
options: It gives the elements unique CSS styling IDs
It helps React's reconciliation algorithm identify which items have changed, been added, or been removed, minimizing DOM mutations
It encrypts the list items in browser memory
It allows elements to be accessed via document.getElementById
questions.explanation: Keys provide stable identities for virtual DOM elements during reconciliation, preventing expensive DOM recreations.

questions.text: When should you use the 'useMemo' hook in React?
options: For every single calculation in a component
To memoize the result of an expensive calculation between re-renders when its inputs have not changed
To perform side effects like fetching data from an API
To replace Redux or global state management
questions.explanation: useMemo caches computation results to avoid unnecessary recalculation on re-renders when dependencies remain unchanged.

questions.text: What is the Virtual DOM in React?
options: A browser plugin for rendering 3D graphics
A lightweight in-memory representation of the real DOM tree used to compute minimal DOM diffs (reconciliation)
A shadow DOM implementation for custom web components
A database table stored in browser IndexedDB
questions.explanation: The Virtual DOM is a JavaScript object tree representation that React diffs against previous renders to batch optimal real DOM updates.

questions.text: What is the difference between an INNER JOIN and a LEFT JOIN in SQL?
options: INNER JOIN returns only rows that have matches in both tables; LEFT JOIN returns all rows from the left table plus matching rows from the right table (with NULLs for non-matches)
INNER JOIN is for strings, LEFT JOIN is for numbers
LEFT JOIN deletes unmatched rows from the database
INNER JOIN is slower in all database engines
questions.explanation: INNER JOIN filters out rows that lack counterparts; LEFT JOIN preserves all left table records regardless of whether a right match exists.

questions.text: What is the difference between the WHERE clause and the HAVING clause in SQL?
options: WHERE filters individual rows before aggregation; HAVING filters groups after GROUP BY aggregation functions have been evaluated
HAVING is used for sorting, WHERE is used for filtering
WHERE only works on primary keys
There is no difference
questions.explanation: WHERE filters source rows before grouping; HAVING filters aggregated groups (e.g. HAVING COUNT(*) > 5).

questions.text: What do the ACID properties stand for in relational database transactions?
options: Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability
Asynchronous, Concurrent, Indexed, Distributed
Availability, Consistency, Integrity, Durability
Authentication, Cryptography, Identity, Delegation
questions.explanation: ACID guarantees that database transactions are processed reliably: all or nothing (Atomic), valid state (Consistent), independent (Isolated), and persistent (Durable).

questions.text: What does a B-Tree index on a database column do to improve query performance?
options: Compresses table data on disk
Allows the database engine to find specific rows in O(log n) time without scanning every row in the table (Full Table Scan)
Prevents any write operations to the table
Automatically executes queries in parallel on multiple GPUs
questions.explanation: B-Tree indexes maintain a balanced tree structure that reduces lookup time from O(n) table scans to O(log n) lookups.

questions.text: How do you prevent SQL Injection vulnerabilities when executing queries with user inputs in applications?
options: Concatenate strings with single quotes
Use parameterized queries (prepared statements) that separate SQL code from user-supplied data
Convert all user input to uppercase letters
Run queries only inside a try-catch block
questions.explanation: Parameterized queries ensure user input is treated strictly as data literals and never interpreted as executable SQL syntax.

questions.text: What is the key difference between 'git merge' and 'git rebase'?
options: 'git merge' creates a 3-way merge commit preserving true branch topology; 'git rebase' rewrites commit history by moving commits onto the tip of another branch for a linear history
'git rebase' deletes the source branch permanently
'git merge' can only be run once per repository
'git rebase' cannot resolve conflicts
questions.explanation: Merge preserves non-linear history with a merge commit; rebase replays your commits atop the target branch, creating new commit SHAs.

questions.text: What does 'git cherry-pick <commit-hash>' do?
options: Deletes that specific commit from the remote repository
Applies the changes introduced by an existing commit from another branch onto the current working branch
Reverts the entire commit history back to that commit
Creates a new tag at that commit
questions.explanation: Cherry-pick selects a specific commit by hash and replays its diff onto the currently checked-out branch.

questions.text: What is a 'detached HEAD' state in Git?
options: A state where Git is corrupted and cannot commit changes
When HEAD points directly to a specific commit SHA rather than to a named branch reference
When remote origin has been disconnected
When a rebase has completed without errors
questions.explanation: Detached HEAD means HEAD references a commit directly (e.g. git checkout <hash>), so new commits aren't associated with any branch unless you create one.

questions.text: What is the difference between 'git reset --soft' and 'git reset --hard'?
options: '--soft' moves HEAD back but leaves changes staged in the index; '--hard' moves HEAD and completely discards all staged and working directory changes
'--hard' creates a backup commit, '--soft' does not
'--soft' deletes uncommitted files
There is no difference in Git
questions.explanation: git reset --soft rewinds the commit history but preserves changes in the staging index; --hard obliterates working directory modifications.

questions.text: What command temporarily shelves uncommitted local changes so you can pull or switch branches on a clean working directory?
options: git stash
git pause
git freeze
git archive
questions.explanation: git stash saves dirty working directory state to a local stack and reverts back to HEAD; use 'git stash pop' to restore changes.

questions.text: According to Eric Brewer's CAP Theorem, what fundamental guarantee must a distributed system make when a network partition (P) occurs?
options: It must guarantee both full Consistency (C) and 100% Availability (A) simultaneously
It must choose between Consistency (returning an error or waiting) or Availability (returning stale data)
It must immediately shut down all nodes across all availability zones
It must switch from TCP to UDP communication
questions.explanation: When network partitions occur, systems must choose between Consistency (CP) or Availability (AP).

questions.text: In the Raft consensus algorithm, how does a cluster maintain consistent state and handle leader failures?
options: Nodes choose random leader IDs without communication
Followers use randomized election timeouts to transition to candidates and seek majority votes from a quorum of nodes
The node with the lowest IP address is permanently designated as the sole leader
Transactions are recorded in plaintext files without log replication
questions.explanation: Raft uses randomized election timeouts and requires a strict quorum for leader election and log commits.

questions.text: When coordinating a multi-step business workflow across multiple independent microservices, why is the Saga pattern preferred over 2-Phase Commit (2PC)?
options: 2PC is lock-free and has no latency overhead

2PC holds locks across all participating services until the final commit, causing high latency, single points of failure, and poor scalability under load; Sagas use asynchronous local transactions and compensating actions
Sagas require synchronous HTTP connections between all microservices
The Saga pattern only works on single-node relational databases
questions.explanation: 2PC is blocking and fragile across networks; Sagas execute local transactions with compensating rollbacks.

questions.text: What is the purpose of an 'Idempotency Key' in distributed message processing and payment APIs?
options: To encrypt payload contents in transit using TLS 1.3
To allow clients to safely retry requests without fear of executing duplicate transactions or side effects when network timeouts occur
To force consumer threads to process messages in chronological order
To generate dynamic API documentation
questions.explanation: Idempotency keys prevent duplicate execution when network retries occur.

questions.text: In distributed key-value stores without synchronized physical wall clocks, how are concurrent update conflicts detected across replicas?
options: By relying strictly on server system clocks (NTP timestamps)
By using logical clocks or Vector Clocks to capture causality and detect concurrent branching updates
By discarding all writes that occur after 12:00 UTC
By pinging the client browser for the current local time
questions.explanation: Vector Clocks track causal relationships across nodes to detect concurrent branching conflicts.

questions.text: Why are multi-stage Docker builds widely used in production CI/CD pipelines?
options: To run multiple containers inside the same single Docker image
To separate build-time dependencies from the final lean runtime image, minimizing image size and attack surface
To bypass Docker layer caching completely
To automatically publish images to Docker Hub without authentication
questions.explanation: Multi-stage builds leave compilers and build tooling behind, producing minimal runtime images.

questions.text: In Kubernetes, what is the fundamental difference between a 'Deployment' and a 'StatefulSet'?
options: Deployments are only for Linux nodes, while StatefulSets are only for Windows nodes
Deployments manage interchangeable, stateless replicas with ephemeral storage, whereas StatefulSets maintain sticky pod identities, ordered rollouts, and persistent volume bindings
StatefulSets do not support rolling updates or autoscaling
Deployments cannot expose network ports
questions.explanation: StatefulSets provide stable network IDs and dedicated persistent volume bindings for stateful services.

questions.text: Which Kubernetes Service type creates an internal virtual IP accessible ONLY within the cluster network?
options: NodePort
LoadBalancer
ClusterIP
ExternalName
questions.explanation: ClusterIP is the default internal-only service type.

questions.text: How does Kubernetes Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA) scale workloads dynamically in production?
options: By adjusting pod CPU clock speeds on the underlying nodes
By querying the metrics server and adjusting the Deployment's replica count within min/max bounds
By automatically rewriting Dockerfiles at runtime
By terminating unhealthy worker nodes
questions.explanation: HPA queries metrics server and adjusts replica counts automatically.

questions.text: Why should instructions that change frequently (like 'COPY . .') be placed near the BOTTOM of a Dockerfile?
options: Because Docker executes files from bottom to top
To maximize layer cache reuse for earlier steps (like installing dependencies), avoiding redundant dependency downloads when only source code changes
Because the Linux kernel requires application code to reside on the root partition
To prevent Docker images from exceeding 100MB
questions.explanation: Docker layer caching is invalidated at the changed instruction and all subsequent layers.

questions.text: In the standard Cache-Aside (Lazy Loading) caching pattern, what sequence of actions does the application take on a cache MISS?
options: Throw an HTTP 404 error immediately to the client
Query the primary database, write the retrieved data to the Redis cache with an appropriate TTL, and return the result to the caller
Flush all keys in Redis and restart the database service
Block until another client populates the key
questions.explanation: On cache miss, app reads DB, sets Redis key with TTL, and returns response.

questions.text: Which Redis eviction policy should you configure if you want Redis to automatically evict the least recently used keys among ONLY those with an expiration (TTL) set?
options: noeviction
allkeys-lru
volatile-lru
allkeys-random
questions.explanation: volatile-lru evicts keys based on LRU out of keys with TTL set.

questions.text: Which Redis native data structure is ideally suited for building real-time gaming leaderboards or prioritized job queues?
options: Hashes (HSET)
Sorted Sets (ZSET)
HyperLogLog
Strings (SET)
questions.explanation: Sorted Sets (ZSET) store unique members sorted by numeric scores.

questions.text: How can a distributed lock be safely acquired in Redis using a single atomic command?
options: Run GET key followed by SET key value
Execute 'SET resource_name my_random_token NX PX 30000'
Execute FLUSHALL ASYNC
Call HSETNX on an integer counter
questions.explanation: SET NX PX provides atomic lock acquisition with TTL.

questions.text: What is the key difference between Redis RDB snapshots and AOF (Append Only File) persistence?
options: RDB logs every write operation in real-time, while AOF only runs when Redis shuts down
RDB creates point-in-time binary snapshots at specified intervals, while AOF logs every write operation sequentially for maximum durability
RDB requires a relational database backend, while AOF stores data in browser memory
AOF is only supported on single-threaded ARM processors
questions.explanation: RDB creates point-in-time dumps; AOF logs every write command sequentially.

questions.text: In cloud architecture, what does deploying a web application across multiple Availability Zones (Multi-AZ) within a region primarily achieve?
options: Zero networking costs between cloud providers
High Availability (HA) and fault tolerance against power, cooling, or hardware failures in an individual data center
Compliance with local data sovereignty laws across different countries
Automatic conversion of monolithic code to microservices
questions.explanation: Multi-AZ provides redundancy across isolated physical data center facilities.

questions.text: According to the Twelve-Factor App methodology for modern cloud applications, how should configuration (such as database credentials and API keys) be stored?
options: Hardcoded directly into the application source code repository
Injected via Environment Variables at container startup time
Checked into public Git commits inside config.json
Stored on local USB drives attached to each hypervisor
questions.explanation: Factor III dictates storing config in environment variables.

questions.text: In Cloud Disaster Recovery planning, what is the precise distinction between RTO (Recovery Time Objective) and RPO (Recovery Point Objective)?
options: RTO measures acceptable downtime until service is restored; RPO measures the maximum acceptable age of data lost due to the disaster
RTO measures cloud server costs; RPO measures database read queries per second
RPO measures downtime in minutes; RTO measures network bandwidth in Gbps
They are synonymous metrics measuring memory usage
questions.explanation: RTO is target restoration time; RPO is maximum acceptable data loss in time.

questions.text: Within a Virtual Private Cloud (VPC), where should production database instances be placed for enterprise security?
options: In a public subnet with a public IPv4 address and 0.0.0.0/0 ingress enabled
In an isolated private subnet with no direct public route, accessible only via internal application servers or a bastion host / VPN
Directly on the Edge CDN distribution point
Inside the DNS nameserver records
questions.explanation: Databases belong in private subnets without public internet routes.

questions.text: What problem does the Circuit Breaker pattern solve in distributed cloud microservices?
options: It automatically encrypts traffic using asymmetric RSA keys
It prevents cascading failures by stopping requests to an already failing upstream dependency, allowing it time to recover while returning fast fallback responses
It powers down servers at night to save cloud infrastructure costs
It synchronizes client clock drift with atomic standards
questions.explanation: Circuit Breakers trip open during downstream failure, avoiding cascading thread exhaustion.

deep_explanation.elevator_pitch: PulseAI Diagnostic is purpose-built to solve core bottlenecks in HealthTech & Clinical AI. Based on the thesis: 'AI-powered medical triage platform for rural health clinics with low connectivity.', it introduces an autonomous AI workflow engine that eliminates manual friction, cuts operational overhead by 70%, and provides verifiable data transparency.
deep_explanation.architectural_thesis: The software architecture utilizes HIPAA-compliant FastAPI backend, encrypted PostgreSQL with audit logging, fine-tuned medical reasoning models, and WebRTC tele-triage. High availability is achieved through stateless API containers, microsecond relational reads, and asynchronous task execution.
deep_explanation.core_value_prop: Replaces fragmented legacy spreadsheets and disconnected point solutions with a unified, end-to-end autonomous intelligent platform offering instant time-to-value within 48 hours.
deep_explanation.monetization_strategy: B2B SaaS tiered subscription model with Starter ($499/mo), Professional ($1,999/mo), and Enterprise Custom ($5,000+/mo with custom SLAs and white-glove onboarding).
deep_explanation.defensibility_moat: High data gravity through continuous workflow ingestion, proprietary model calibration, and sticky multi-stakeholder network effects that create high switching costs.

mvp_features: Core autonomous ingestion pipeline connecting existing customer workflows.
Real-time analytics dashboard with interactive data visualizers.
Automated PDF report and proposal generation engine.
Role-based authentication with strict data isolation and audit logging.
phase2_features: Multi-agent predictive simulation and automated scenario forecasting.
Native two-way ERP and enterprise software integrations (SAP, Salesforce, Slack).
Advanced collaborative team workspaces with approval hierarchies.
target_icp: Mid-to-large enterprise department leads, VP of Technology, and Chief Operating Officers.
High-growth startups and scaling businesses seeking operational leverage.

risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Enforce SOC2 Type II, encrypted credential storage, and Row Level Security.

FastAPI hosting, managed PostgreSQL clusters, LLM token credits, and DDoS protection.

deep_explanation.architectural_thesis: The software architecture utilizes HIPAA-compliant FastAPI backend, encrypted PostgreSQL with audit logging, fine-tuned medical reasoning models, and WebRTC tele-triage. High availability is achieved through stateless API containers, microsecond relational reads, and asynchronous task execution.
deep_explanation.core_value_prop: Replaces fragmented legacy spreadsheets and disconnected point solutions with a unified, end-to-end autonomous intelligent platform offering instant time-to-value within 48 hours.
deep_explanation.monetization_strategy: B2B SaaS tiered subscription model with Starter ($499/mo), Professional ($1,999/mo), and Enterprise Custom ($5,000+/mo with custom SLAs and white-glove onboarding).
deep_explanation.defensibility_moat: High data gravity through continuous workflow ingestion, proprietary model calibration, and sticky multi-stakeholder network effects that create high switching costs.

Role-based authentication with strict data isolation and audit logging.
